title: RiskShard source audit
description: ADR-0015. What each registered source publishes, audited on four properties. The load-bearing rule is structural rather than conventional: a claim about a source may only be published when its basis is verified_against_artifact. `derived_from_corpus` is a fact about our own extraction and is never evidence about the source.

artifact_sha256.description: The sha256 of the artifact read, as recorded in sources/manifest.json. Required on any verified answer. The hash rather than a path because sources/raw/ is not distributed (large, third-party PDFs): a path is only recheckable on the machine that holds the file, while a hash identifies the exact document anyone can re-fetch from the manifest's URL. It also pins the edition — a new edition of the same title has a different hash and does not inherit this answer.

artifact.description: Convenience path under sources/raw/, for a reader who has gathered the corpus. Never load-bearing — artifact_sha256 is.

basis.description: verified_against_artifact: a human read the stored artifact — the only basis a source-level claim may rest on. derived_from_corpus: what our extraction shows, a fact about us. unverified: not yet read; the default, and the work queue. no_readable_artifact: the gathered artifact is not the source — a landing page, a news summary, a paywall — so the question cannot be answered until the document itself is obtained. Distinct from unverified on purpose: 'we have not read it' and 'we cannot read it' are different states, and collapsing them would let a permanent gap masquerade as a backlog.

publishes.description: Does the source publish this? Meaningful only when basis is verified_against_artifact; forbidden otherwise, so an unread source cannot carry an answer that reads as read.

detail.description: What was found, in the source's own terms — the page, table or figure, or the phrase that settles it.

verified_on.description: ISO date the artifact was read. Required with verified_against_artifact: an edition can change what a source publishes.

corpus_note.description: For derived_from_corpus only: what our own extraction shows. Never phrased as a statement about the source.

allOf.$comment: ADR-0015 part 2 made structural: only a verified answer may assert what the source publishes, and it must say when it was read.
A corpus-derived note is a fact about our extraction; it has no place on a verified or unread answer.
